title: Intermediate Backend Engineer, Authorization
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.
Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.
You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.
Some examples of our projects:
Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service
Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design
What you'll do
Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access.
Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers.
Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog.
Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently.
Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers.
Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions.
Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service.
Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more.
Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects.
A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation.
Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior.
Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns.
Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request.
Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting.
Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture.
We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.
About the team
We work in a fully asynchronous organization, with most decisions made in documents or merge requests rather than meetings.
GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our values include collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency. We expect all GitLab team members to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.
Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.
We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.
What you'll do
Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.
About the team
The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.
At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

An overview of this role
As a Data Engineer at GitLab, you'll build, run, and maintain the pipelines and infrastructure that bring data from our enterprise applications, internal systems, and GitLab's software as a service (SaaS) platform into our data platform. Your work will power company reporting, data science, and artificial intelligence (AI) self-service.
You'll own features end to end, from source integration to tested, monitored, documented data ready for use. You'll focus on keeping the platform reliable, secure, and cost-efficient as data volumes and AI usage grow, and making governed data ready for AI tools, agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based access. This is an AI-first role: you'll use AI coding agents every day while maintaining high standards for code review and testing. You'll report to the Director, Data Platform.
What you’ll do
Build, extend, and maintain extract, load, transform (ELT) pipelines from enterprise applications such as Salesforce, Zuora, Zendesk, and Marketo, internal systems, and the GitLab SaaS platform. Integrate data through application programming interfaces (APIs) and event sources such as Snowplow.
Manage and maintain the infrastructure behind the platform, including SaaS tools such as Snowflake, Fivetran, and Monte Carlo, and self-managed services such as Airflow and Kubernetes.
Write maintainable, well-tested, performant Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) code that meets our internal standards, and review GitLab team members' merge requests.
Own day-to-day platform operations: triage and resolve failed pipelines, infrastructure issues, and GitLab team member requests. Use monitoring, service-level agreements (SLAs), data contracts, query and warehouse tuning, and data quality checks to keep the platform reliable and cost-efficient.
Partner with Analytics Engineers, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Data Governance, and business partners so data lands in the shape they need for downstream use.
Use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, OpenCode, GitLab Duo, or similar tools to speed up development, debugging, testing, and documentation without compromising review rigor.
Apply role-based access control (RBAC) and masking policies to make governed data available to AI tools and agents. Handle data subject to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls, material nonpublic information (MNPI), and personal data safely.
Ship medium-sized features independently in small, iterative merge requests, and document architecture and runbooks in the handbook.
What You'll Bring
Professional experience shipping production data pipelines in Python.
Deep, hands-on SQL skills and experience with a cloud data warehouse; Snowflake is preferred.
Hands-on experience with ELT or extract, transform, load (ETL) pipelines at scale, including incremental loads, schema changes, backfills, and API ingestion.
Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow, familiarity with dbt, and solid data modeling fundamentals, including Kimball dimensional modeling.
Experience running and troubleshooting data infrastructure, with comfort using Git-based workflows, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and code review.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools in your daily work, with an understanding of where they help and where they fall short.
Clear written communication, the ability to use GitLab, and comfort working asynchronously in a fully remote organization in line with GitLab's values.
Preferred, not required: experience with Snowflake; Docker, Kubernetes, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Terraform; SaaS application APIs such as Salesforce, Zuora, or Zendesk; data observability tooling; or Snowflake administration.
About the team
The Data Platform team within Enterprise Data is responsible for a scalable, reliable and secure data platform for data analytics at GitLab. That includes managing and maintaining the infrastructure we use, both SaaS and self-managed, and building and maintaining the data pipelines that bring data into it. We make data reliable, secure and ready for analytics, data science and AI tools. As more questions go straight to AI tools and agents, the platform underneath has to be more reliable, better governed and more cost-efficient than ever. We're fully remote and globally distributed, and work asynchronously through issues, merge requests and the handbook.

title: Applied AI Architect
description:
About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping large enterprises understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.
Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems.
Key responsibilities
Partner with account executives across South Korea to deeply understand customer requirements and translate them into technical solutions, ensuring alignment between business objectives and technical implementation
Serve as the primary technical advisor to enterprise customers across South Korea throughout their Claude adoption journey, from discovery to initial evaluation through deployment. You will need to coordinate internally across multiple teams & stakeholders to drive customer success
Support customers building with both the Claude API and Claude for Work
Create and deliver compelling technical content tailored to different audiences across South Korea. You will need to be able to run the gamut from technical deep dives for engineering & development teams up to business value focused conversations with executives
Guide technical architecture decisions and help customers across South Korea integrate Claude effectively into their existing technology stack
Help customers develop evaluation frameworks to measure Claude's performance for their specific use cases
Identify common integration patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams
Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops, technical deep dives, and relationship building
Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities and implementation patterns
Minimum qualifications
Experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager
Native-level Korean fluency and business-level English required
Experience working with enterprise customers, navigating complex buying cycles involving multiple stakeholders
Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more
Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate customer requirements between technical and business stakeholders
Preferred qualifications
5+ years of relevant experience
Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems
Comfortable with python
Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science
Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems
Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

description:
About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic Australia, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping large enterprises across Australia and the Asia-Pacific region understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.
Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems.
Responsibilities:
Partner with account executives to deeply understand customer requirements and translate them into technical solutions, ensuring alignment between business objectives and technical implementation
Serve as the primary technical advisor to enterprise customers throughout their Claude adoption journey, from discovery to initial evaluation through deployment. You will need to coordinate internally across multiple teams & stakeholders to drive customer success
Support customers building with both the Claude API and Claude for Work
Create and deliver compelling technical content tailored to different audiences. You will need to be able to spread the gamut from technical deep dives for engineering & development teams up to business value focused conversations with executives
Guide technical architecture decisions and help customers integrate Claude effectively into their existing technology stack
Help customers develop evaluation frameworks to measure Claude's performance for their specific use cases
Identify common integration patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams
Travel occasionally within Australia and the APAC region to customer sites for workshops, technical deep dives, and relationship building
Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities and implementation patterns
Collaborate across time zones with global teams while serving as the technical expert for the Australia market
You may be a good fit if you have:
10+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager
Experience working with enterprise customers in Australia or the APAC region, navigating complex buying cycles involving multiple stakeholders
Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more
Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate customer requirements between technical and business stakeholders
Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems
Comfortable with Python
Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science
Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems
Ability to work effectively across cultures and time zones as part of a global team
Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Build reusable assets (reference designs, connectors, prompt and eval templates) so one partner's work helps the next.

Clear written and spoken communication across a broad audience. The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to epidemiologists, program leads, field teams and executives.
Patience with long buying cycles, a knack for knowing how to make them go smoothly, and real care for public benefit.
Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As a Partners Solutions Architect on the Applied AI team at Anthropic, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on cultivating technical relationships with our Global and Regional System Integrators (GSIs/RSIs), and our cloud partners . You will strengthen our relationships with key partners to accelerate indirect revenue, enable their AI practices, and execute on long-term GTM strategy.
Responsibilities:
Strategic Technical Partnership: Be a technical thought partner to the Anthropic GTM partnerships team, providing technical expertise to better understand the partner landscape, driving key strategic programs, and identifying opportunities to deepen partner technical capabilities. Embed with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, support troubleshooting, evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities, and serve as an escalation point for complex technical issues.
Joint Solution Development: Collaborate with partners to identify high value industry-specific GenAI applications, develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures / best practices to accelerate time to deployment
Customer Deal Support: Intervene directly to unblock strategic customer deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep technical expertise and solution architecture guidance.
Partner Ecosystem & Events: Represent Anthropic at partner events such as GSI customer workshops, summits, and industry conferences. Lead or support partner-specific developer events, hackathons, and technical enablement sessions, especially for technically native communities.
Product Feedback: Validate and gather feedback on Anthropic's products and offerings, especially as they relate to partner use cases and deployment patterns, and deliver this feedback to relevant Anthropic teams to inform product roadmap and partner strategy.
You may be a good fit if you have:
10+ years of experience in technical customer-facing/partner-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner Sales Engineer
Track record of successfully partnering with GSIs and/or cloud providers to solve complex technical challenges, from initial solution design through customer delivery
Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more
Strong presentation & technical communication skills with the ability to translate requirements between technical and business stakeholders
Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems
Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science
Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities
A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed
Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems
Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
 
The Role
 
The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP.
 
You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software.
 
A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.
Technologies We Use
Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms
Core Responsibilities
Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.
What We Value
An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.
What We Require
4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.
Salary
 
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.
 
Life at Palantir
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
 
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.

Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg

Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

Curiosity about how data connection systems work, from productized connectors to the infrastructure required to run them
An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
Comfort following problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments
Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience
Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Python, or Go
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Coursework, projects, or practical experience in one or more of computer networks, distributed systems, databases, cloud computing, or software architecture.
Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.
To apply, please submit the following:
An updated resume / CV - please do so in PDF format.
Thoughtful responses to our application questions.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer, you will partner directly with Digital Native companies to design, build and deploy AI-powered products and systems. Working alongside customer product and engineering teams, you will take ideas from early experimentation through evaluation, production launch and scale, connecting technical decisions to user experience and measurable business impact.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with Digital Native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

title: EDA Cloud & Developer Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.

The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.

In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.

This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.

In this role, you will:

 - Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.

 - Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.

 - Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.

 - Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.

 - Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.

 - Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.

 - Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with proficiency in Python or a similar programming language and experience building reliable automation, tools, or infrastructure services.

 - Bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of infrastructure engineering, such as Linux/HPC environments, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, storage, networking, or EDA development workflows.

 - Have experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud infrastructure, preferably Azure, with familiarity in infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Bicep.

 - Have strong Linux systems knowledge, including processes, filesystems, networking, permissions, performance troubleshooting, and system administration.

 - Have experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms.

 - Are comfortable debugging complex distributed infrastructure problems, identifying root causes, and implementing durable solutions.

 - Enjoy working closely with engineering teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into scalable, practical infrastructure solutions.

 - Take ownership of systems end to end, from initial design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing operational improvements.

 - Bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to solving ambiguous engineering challenges.

 - Are curious about hardware development and excited to expand your technical expertise across infrastructure, silicon design workflows, and developer productivity.

Bonus Qualifications

 - Experience supporting ASIC or semiconductor development environments, including EDA workflows, design verification, physical design, emulation, or formal verification.

 - Experience operating large-scale HPC clusters or workload schedulers such as Slurm.

 - Familiarity with compute farms, regression frameworks, build systems, and hardware development toolchains.

 - Experience with enterprise identity and authentication systems, such as Entra ID, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA, or SSSD.

 - Experience designing and operating relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design, migrations, query optimization, and backups.

 - Familiarity with distributed systems components, including message queues, caching layers, artifact storage, and backend services.

 - Experience with high-performance storage systems, data movement optimization, or large-scale compute infrastructure.

 - Experience managing EDA license servers, license utilization, or other shared infrastructure resources in hardware development environments.

title: Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Strategic Finance Data Science team helps OpenAI understand business performance and make informed decisions about growth, revenue, and resource allocation. We partner with Strategic Finance, Data Engineering, and business teams to build trusted metrics, explain what is changing, and support forecasting, planning, pricing, and investment decisions.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement to turn complex financial and business questions into reliable data products, clear analyses, and actionable recommendations. You will work across the analytical workflow: define the question, establish trustworthy metrics and datasets, investigate the drivers, and help partners act on the findings.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will combine the technical depth of analytics engineering with strong analytical judgment and close partnership with Strategic Finance. Your work will serve both executive reviews and the teams making day-to-day business decisions.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Define and maintain trusted metrics and analytical datasets for revenue, usage, customer performance, compute consumption, and margin, with clear definitions and appropriate product, customer, and cohort detail.

 - Build automated dashboards and recurring reporting that help Finance leaders and operating teams understand performance, spot changes, and prioritize investigation.

 - Explain movements in business results and variances against expectations by examining underlying drivers, validating data quality, and distinguishing evidence from assumptions.

 - Translate ambiguous questions about growth, retention, monetization, pricing, and resource efficiency into structured analyses and practical recommendations.

 - Partner with forecasting specialists and Finance to provide reliable inputs, driver analyses, and scenario assumptions for forecasts and long-range plans.

 - Work with Data Engineering to improve the quality and usability of underlying data, and develop reusable analytical models and workflows that reduce manual effort.

 - Communicate findings clearly, align stakeholders on trade-offs, and follow through to understand whether the analysis or data product improved the decision.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have strong SQL and analytical data-modeling skills, and experience turning large, complex datasets into reliable analyses and reusable data products.

 - Can reason carefully about metrics, cohorts, denominators, measurement changes, and uncertainty, and investigate whether an unexpected result reflects the business or the data.

 - Have built dashboards or recurring reporting used by business partners, and can explain the decisions they enabled.

 - Bring sound business judgment and can independently scope an ambiguous problem, prioritize the work, and deliver an end-to-end solution.

 - Communicate technical findings clearly and work effectively with Finance, data scientists, engineers, and other business partners.

 - Can use Python or a comparable analytical tool to investigate data and automate repetitive work.

The Consulting team is part of OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. Our goal is to help consulting teams do better work for their clients. We work side by side with design partners to understand how their teams operate, then use what we learn to build for consultants everywhere.

Today, we’re bringing OpenAI’s models and products together to accelerate the core work of consulting, from investigating a client’s question to delivering advice they can act on. We’re starting by removing the barriers that keep consultants from using AI in their day-to-day work. We’ll draw on the full range of OpenAI’s capabilities, from ChatGPT Work to newer tools such as Dots and Spaces.

Longer term, we want to help firms develop AI-native ways of working. A team could design an engagement around questions it can now afford to explore, test several strategies with its client, and change course as it learns what works. We’re moving quickly, working across OpenAI’s research, product, and engineering teams to turn what we learn with design partners into products consultants everywhere can use.

We’re looking for a full-stack software engineer to build first-party OpenAI products for consulting. You’ll own features end to end, from the frontend interfaces consultants use to the backend services and integrations that power them.

title: Software Engineer, Guardian
description:
About the Team

The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm.

Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products.

Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group.



About the Role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the Guardian team in London. You will design and build production systems that evaluate agent behavior, identify risk, and take appropriate action without creating unnecessary friction for users.

This is a hands-on engineering role with substantial technical depth and ownership. You will work across architecture, implementation, evaluation, and operations, taking projects from early exploration through production deployment. The work requires strong engineering fundamentals, sound product judgment, and comfort solving problems where both the requirements and the underlying technology are evolving.

You will work closely with alignment researchers to translate emerging research into dependable systems, and with product and engineering teams to make agent safety a foundational capability across OpenAI.

This role is based in our London office.



In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate core components of Auto-review and the broader Guardian platform, balancing safety, product utility, latency, and operational reliability.

 - Build production systems that evaluate agent actions in real time, detect potentially harmful behavior, and support safe recovery or escalation paths.

 - Improve how oversight systems understand user intent, environmental context, permissions, and relevant personalization signals while protecting privacy and avoiding unnecessary friction.

 - Partner closely with alignment researchers to turn prototypes, evaluations, and new monitoring techniques into scalable product capabilities.

 - Work across Product, Security, Infrastructure, and other engineering teams to integrate Guardian capabilities into agent experiences throughout OpenAI.

 - Develop evaluations, adversarial tests, and monitoring to understand safety performance, false positives, latency, and user impact.

 - Own projects end to end, contribute to technical direction and design reviews, and investigate failures to improve system behavior and reliability.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience building and shipping complex production software, with ownership across design, implementation, deployment, and operation.

 - Have built with AI agents or large language models in a core product, startup, or technically serious independent project, and understand the unique challenges of agentic systems.

 - Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and can design reliable backend services, APIs, and infrastructure.

 - Exercise sound product-engineering judgment and can navigate tradeoffs across safety, usability, speed, and reliability.

 - Enjoy working closely with researchers, translating open-ended ideas into practical systems, and using experiments and evaluations to guide decisions.

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity, take initiative, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines.

 - Care deeply about building AI systems that are useful, trustworthy, and safe.

The Agent Platform team at OpenAI builds the production systems that bring useful AI agents to users around the world. We provide the platform that enables agents to execute code, use tools, and interact with software reliably and securely at scale.

We work closely with product, research, and infrastructure teams to turn new agent capabilities into dependable product experiences. Our work spans the execution environments, APIs, and integrations that support agentic products such as Codex and tool use in ChatGPT.

title: Applied AI Architect, Cyber

We act as trusted technical advisors and thought partners for customers, working side by side with their teams to identify high-value use cases, design practical architectures, and move from prototype to durable deployment.

Cybersecurity is one of the most urgent domains where AI can help. Security teams are under pressure to reason across code, logs, infrastructure, tickets, alerts, and vulnerability data faster than ever. As frontier models become more capable, organizations need deep technical guidance on how to evaluate, validate, and safely deploy AI systems in security-critical workflows.

You will help customers evaluate and deploy workflows such as secure code review, vulnerability triage, threat modeling, remediation, SOC and incident response workflows, detection engineering, cloud security, GRC automation, and security validation.

You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Research, and Security to turn customer needs into safe deployment patterns, reusable field assets, and product feedback.

The Preparedness team is an important part of the Safety Systems https://openai.com/safety/safety-systems org at OpenAI, and is guided by OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/.

Frontier AI models have the potential to benefit all of humanity, but also pose increasingly severe risks. To ensure that AI promotes positive change, the Preparedness team helps us prepare for the development of increasingly capable frontier AI models. This team is tasked with identifying, tracking, and preparing for catastrophic risks related to frontier AI models.

The mission of the Preparedness team is to:

 1. Closely monitor and predict the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems, with an eye towards misuse risks whose impact could be catastrophic to our society

 2. Ensure we have concrete procedures, infrastructure and partnerships to mitigate these risks and to safely handle the development of powerful AI systems

Preparedness tightly connects capability assessment, evaluations, and internal red teaming, and mitigations for frontier models, as well as overall coordination on AGI preparedness. This is fast paced, exciting work that has far reaching importance for the company and for society.

 

About the Role

We’re hiring a Data Scientist to help build, evaluate, and continuously improve mitigations that prevent extreme harms from AI systems. This role is for an experienced, highly autonomous individual contributor who can take ambiguous problem statements, structure rigorous analyses, and translate findings into actionable product and policy changes.

This position goes beyond “running evals.” You’ll help create mitigation intelligence and monitoring systems that enable OpenAI to detect issues early, measure effectiveness over time, and reduce both over-blocking (unnecessary friction) and under-blocking (missed harm).





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Evaluate and improve mitigation systems, including classifiers and detection pipelines across domains (e.g., biosecurity, cybersecurity, and emerging risk areas).

 - Diagnose false positives and false negatives with deep error analysis, root cause investigation, and clear recommendations for mitigation adjustments.

 - Build monitoring and measurement frameworks to track mitigation effectiveness over time and across user segments and use cases.

 - Identify trends in over-blocking vs. under-blocking, quantify customer impact, and propose prioritized interventions.

 - Develop insights from customer feedback, complaints, and usage patterns to detect shifts in adversarial behavior and system failure modes.

 - Expand risk monitoring into new areas, including cybersecurity threats and model loss-of-control or sabotage scenarios, in partnership with domain experts.

 - Communicate results to technical and executive stakeholders with crisp narratives, decision-ready metrics, and clear tradeoffs.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every approval request, receipt reminder, payment alert, and card notification Ramp sends has to reach the right person, on the right channel, at the right time. When it does, finance teams close faster and employees spend less time chasing tasks. When it doesn't, a missed message can mean a stalled approval, a late payment, or a flood of notifications nobody asked for.



Ramp's Communications Platform team builds the shared system that every product team uses to reach customers. It handles transactional messages across email, SMS, push, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp, including templating, delivery, retries, digesting, user preferences, and delivery monitoring. The team also supports the conversational experiences that let customers work with Ramp directly from the channels they already use.



We're looking for a backend engineer to own a core part of that platform. You'll take responsibility for an area such as message delivery and channel integrations, communication preferences, or platform reliability and scale, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and dependable as message volume and the number of teams building on it grow. You'll work closely with product, design, and engineering partners across Ramp to make communications faster, more reliable, and easier for every team to build on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the design and evolution of a core part of Ramp's communications platform, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 - Build and extend integrations with messaging channels and delivery providers, including email, SMS, push, and workplace chat tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams

 - Design delivery workflows that are idempotent, retry safely, and confirm successful delivery, so customers reliably get the messages they need without duplicate sends

 - Build communication preferences and controls that let users and administrators decide what they receive and where

 - Make the platform simple and safe for other Ramp engineers to build on, with clear abstractions, strong defaults, and good developer tooling

 - Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the platform as message volume grows

 - Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

As part of our team, you will turn robot use cases into measurable capability and acceptance goals, covering embodiment constraints, task success, intervention rate, cycle time, plus recovery. title: Expert Engineer - Robotics AI Deployment (f/m/div.)
description:
As part of our team, you will bring up the target embodiment end to end, covering robot interfaces, sensors, calibration, coordinate frames, time synchronization, grippers, as well as control modes. You implement and debug the integration yourself, working across the control stack and embodiment, including ROS 2.
You will integrate world-/video-action models, learned policies, reasoning agents, as well as executable code or graph policies with the control stack. You translate their outputs into validated robot commands and feedback contracts while working with the corresponding model and code/graph-policy runtimes.
Additionally, you will engineer execution across inference and control rates, including action buffering, interpolation, latency, jitter, stale observations, watchdogs, limits, as well as recovery mechanisms. You also profile compute, memory, and communication on target hardware and use hardware-in-the-loop tests to validate the integration.
You will build repeatable physical rollout loops with scene reset, outcome verification, telemetry, as well as failure replay. You support ASPIRE/ENPIRE-style refinement through controlled experiments and explicit release gates, developing robust reset and verification tooling.
Furthermore, you will take ownership of first deployments and staged rollouts without relying on a staffed deployment team. You version software, models, as well as embodiment configurations while implementing regression tests, monitoring, plus rollback in collaboration with safety and security specialists, supported by dedicated deployment and rollout tooling.
Using the Agentic AI Software Factory, you will build integration and test tooling while verifying generated work on hardware. You then feed reproducible failures back into architecture and model development.

Afin de participer activement au développement de nos outils de digitalisation et accompagner les nouveaux projets de l’entreprise, nous recrutons un(e) stagiaire développeur Full Stack qui apportera aux équipes et aux clients, agilité, flexibilité et performance.

title: ServiceNow Developer (f/m)
description:
Designs, builds, and maintains solutions on the ServiceNow enterprise platform across core modules (ITSM, ITOM, HAM, OTSM, Service Portal, and custom scoped applications). Turns business requirements into robust, upgrade-resilient solutions using platform best practices, working as an active member of an Agile squad under the guidance of the Lead Developer and Platform Architect.
Key Responsibilities
Platform Development: Configure and develop features across core modules (e.g. Incident, Problem, Change, Request, Knowledge, and custom scoped apps in ServiceNow Studio / App Engine Studio).
Workflows & Scripting: Build robust automations using Flow Designer, subflows, and actions. Write clean, maintainable server-side and client-side code (Business Rules, Script Includes, Client Scripts, UI Policies).
Service Catalog & Portal: Develop dynamic catalog items, record producers, and order guides with variable sets and fulfillment flows. Build and configure Service Portal and Employee Center widgets.
Integrations: Configure and support REST/SOAP integrations, IntegrationHub spokes, MID Server queries, and import sets with transform maps.
Quality & Agile Delivery: Participate actively in sprint refinement, estimation, and daily standups. Build automated test cases using Automated Test Framework (ATF), participate in peer code reviews, and support UAT bug resolution.
Platform Health: Support semi-annual platform family upgrades by reviewing skipped records and refactoring legacy code back to baseline out-of-the-box (OOTB) functionality.
Experience & Qualifications:
Experience: 3 to 5 years in software engineering, with at least 2 to 3 years of hands-on ServiceNow configuration and development experience.
Technical Skills: Strong JavaScript fundamentals; hands-on proficiency with Glide APIs, Flow Designer, NowAssist, Service Catalog, and REST integrations; solid grasp of the ServiceNow relational data model and ACL security rules.
Methodology: Practical experience working within Scrum/Agile environments (Jira / ServiceNow Agile).
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience.
Certifications:
Required: ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA), Certified Application Developer (CAD).
Preferred: Certified Implementation Specialist in one of ServiceNow product (CIS - ITSM), ITIL 4 Foundation.
