title: Products Analytics Engineer - Internship
description:
We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries.



The team

As a Product Analytics Engineer Intern, you will join the Product Analytics team supporting Ledger Wallet across Product, Business, and Growth/CRM teams. Reporting directly to the Product Data Analytics Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring tracking data quality, and scaling our analytics infrastructure to support company-wide data-driven decision-making.



What you’ll be doing

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Product Managers, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists to deliver insights and support Growth/CRM personalization pipelines.

 - Experimentation & A/B Testing: Specify and support A/B test setups, funnel evaluation, and advanced statistical analysis for product features.

 - AI Governance & Automation: Help establish governance, guardrails, and custom skills for users querying analytics platforms (Mixpanel, Snowflake MCP) via AI tools, and contribute to building end-to-end AI-assisted tracking workflows.

 - Tracking Quality & Investigations: Triage, investigate, and follow up on tracking issues to maintain data sanity.

 - Documentation & Enablement: Develop comprehensive documentation and data models (dbt/data mart) to empower stakeholders

 - Privacy & Compliance: Maintain standard privacy-aware constraints across all data modeling and analytics workflows.



What we're looking for

 - Final-year student in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related technical field seeking an end-of-studies internship.

 - Strong proficiency in SQL, Python scripting, and data modeling concepts.

 - Analytics engineering mindset with a focus on data quality, reliability, reproducibility, and documentation.

 - Understanding of A/B testing methodologies, statistical analysis, and funnel evaluation.

 - Familiarity with Product Analytics tools (e.g., Mixpanel, Amplitude) and data visualization tools is a strong plus

 - Hands-on experience or deep curiosity regarding AI agents and workflow automation is a strong plus.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

 - Interest in Web3, digital assets, and crypto is a plus.



At Ledger, we are dedicated to continually investing in our employees which is why we offer more than just salaries; we provide comprehensive compensation packages that include a wide range of benefits. Here are some of the benefits you can look forward to:

 - Flexible work options - Our hybrid policy allows employees to work from home up to 3 times per week

 - Health & Wellness support - Health and Life Insurance.

 - Financial growth opportunities - Employees can become shareholders in Ledger as well as other financial benefits depending on your country of work.

 - Commuter allowance - Ledger offers a commuter allowance to contribute to your preferred means of transportation.

 - Learning & Development - A comprehensive suite of training solutions providing a personalised learning experience for every employee.

For regionally specific benefits, your Talent Acquisition contact will be able to provide you with more information.

We’re committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need any adjustments or accommodations, just let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

title: Back-End Engineer
description:
WE POWER PEOPLE’S PROGRESS.

At Preply, we’re all about creating life-changing learning experiences. We help people discover the magic of the perfect tutor, craft a personalised learning journey, and stay motivated to keep growing. Our approach is human-led, tech-enabled - and it’s creating real impact.

We’ve just reached unicorn status with a $150M Series D, accelerating our vision to transform education through human-led, AI-enhanced learning. Today, 100,000+ tutors teach 90+ languages to learners in 180 countries - and we’re only getting started. As a category-defining company, we’re shaping what the future of learning looks like at global scale.

Every Preply lesson sparks change, fuels ambition, and drives progress that matters. Joining Preply means helping define the future of education at global scale, and building something that truly matters for millions of people, every day.


MEET THE TEAM!

Join Preply’s Teams and help us power people’s progress through life-changing learning experiences. We’re on a mission to combine the magic of the best tutors with cutting-edge AI to create personalized journeys that keep learners motivated and inspired. Together, we’ll transform how students expand their vocabulary, master conversational fluency, and deepen comprehension - unlocking their full potential and sparking a lifelong love for learning. Are you ready to make an impact? Let’s redefine education!

The Preply Engineering Team provides the tools to help unlock human potential through learning.

We implement A/B tests to prove the value of our initiatives and improve our product based on data and students and tutors feedback. As part of our commitment to ensuring high-quality products, we prioritize monitoring and metrics analysis to identify areas for optimization and ensure our services are performing at their best. 

We are tech-agnostic, meaning we are open to considering candidates with diverse technology backgrounds, such as Java/Spring, Node.js/Express.js, Ruby/Ruby on Rails, Scala/Play, PHP, or Golang.

While Python is our primary programming language, prior experience with it is not mandatory. What truly matters is your enthusiasm for learning Python and your ability to adapt quickly to using it for product development.

At Preply, we release our product 50-60 times per day by leveraging top-notch CI/CD processes. As a fast-growing company we have diverse technical challenges (sometimes we even write about them on our Engineering Blog) that will allow you to develop your skills at scale. 





WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

You will work in a cross-functional team alongside the Product Manager, Product Designer, UX Writers, Data Analytics, Technical Leads, Engineers and other cross-functional team members to deliver engaging features through A/B tests and build top-notch products, including, but not limited to:

 - Develop and own backend features using Python/Django, supporting the creation of new backend services as well as design, create, and/or troubleshoot integrations with third-party vendors.

 - Think beyond the code and about our customers, understand their needs and define solutions with the team;

 - Balance short-term speed of development with the long-term technical quality of our systems;

 - As a Back-End Engineer, you will leverage your experience to guide the team in making informed technical decisions, such as continuous improvement of best practices (test culture, code reviews, monitoring and scalability of our tools). 



WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

 - Exposure to architectural patterns of a large, high-scale web application (e.g., well-designed APIs, high-volume data pipelines, efficient algorithms);

 - Familiar and willing to support small JS/TS tasks when needed;

 - Expertise in troubleshooting issues, identifying the root cause, mitigating it, and adding setting up safeguards to prevent future issues;

 - High level of self-organization, ownership, and responsibility;

 - A great collaborator with excellent verbal and written communication skills. Minimum B2 English level;

 - Willingness to be on-call for your squad (1 week every 5 weeks).



WHY YOU’LL LOVE IT AT PREPLY

 - An open, collaborative, dynamic and diverse culture;

 - A generous monthly allowance for lessons on Preply.com http://preply.com/, Learning & Development budget and time off for your self-development;

 - A competitive financial package with equity, leave allowance and health insurance;

 - Not in Barcelona? We offer an attractive relocation package to join us in our Preply Barcelona Hub;

 - Access to free mental health support platforms;

 - Access to Gympass-partnered wellness and gym centers throughout Spain to promote and support well-being and physical health;

 - The opportunity to shape the lives of learners and tutors through language learning and teaching in 175 countries (and counting!).


OUR PRINCIPLES

 - Care to change the world - We are passionate about our work and care deeply about its impact to be life changing.

 - We do it for learners - For both Preply and tutors, learners are why we do what we do. Every day we focus on empowering tutors to deliver an exceptional learning experience.

 - Keep perfecting - To create an outstanding customer experience, we focus on simplicity, smoothness, and enjoyment, continually perfecting it as every detail matters.

 - Now is the time - In a fast-paced world, it matters how quickly we act. Now is the time to make great things happen.

 - Disciplined execution - What makes us disciplined is the excellence in our execution. We set clear goals, focus on what matters, and utilize our resources efficiently.

 - Dive deep - We leverage business acumen and curiosity to investigate disparities between numbers and stories, unlocking meaningful insights to guide our decisions.

 - Growth mindset - We proactively seek growth opportunities and believe today's best performance becomes tomorrow's starting point. We humbly embrace feedback and learn from setbacks.

 - Raise the bar - We raise our performance standards continuously, alongside each new hire and promotion. We build diverse and high-performing teams that can make a real difference.

 - Challenge, disagree and commit - We value open and candid communication, even when we don’t fully agree. We speak our minds, challenge when necessary, and fully commit to decisions once made.

 - One Preply - We prioritize collaboration, inclusion, and the success of our team over personal ambitions. Together, we support and celebrate each other's progress.


DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

Preply.com http://Preply.com is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people of diverse backgrounds can thrive. We believe that the presence of different opinions and viewpoints is a key ingredient for our success as a multicultural Ed-Tech company. That means that Preply will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or veteran status.

title: Junior Managers Program (Trainee) - Starte deine Leadership Journey im Bereich HR Tech, Digitalisierung und Generative AI
description:
Gestalte das Personalwesen der Zukunft mit uns! Wir suchen Master-Graduates mit Gestaltungswillen, die im Junior Managers Program unser HR-Netzwerk revolutionieren und Generative AI (GenAI) in die People-Themen einbringen. Du denkst innovativ, handelst menschenzentriert und willst die besten HR-Tech-Lösungen für Bosch gestalten? Dann möchten wir von dir hören.​
Über eine intensive Reise von 12–24 Monaten wirst du Teil eines der wichtigsten Hebel im Unternehmen: dem Personalbereich. Du rotierst durch verschiedene Bereiche – in Deutschland und weltweit – und tauchst tief ein in HR-Tech, strategische HR Top-Projekte und die Spezialisierung auf GenAI. Deine Mission: Technologie und Mensch zusammenbringen, Prozesse optimieren und HR neu denken.​
Du wirst nicht nur unterstützen – du wirst gestalten, entscheiden und implementieren. Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, führst Projekte und siehst direkt, welchen Impact deine Entscheidungen auf die Candidate und Employee Journeys haben – auf Prozesse, Qualität und Innovation.​
Was du bei uns lernen und entwickeln wirst:​
Du lernst, wie strategisches und operatives HR in einem globalen Technologieunternehmen wirklich funktioniert – und wie Daten, Technologie und Verhandlungsgeschick den Unterschied machen.​
Du gestaltest aktiv HR-Tech-Strategien, entwickelst zukunftsweisende HR-Prozesse weiter und bringst GenAI-Lösungen (wie Chatbots oder automatisierte Analysen) direkt in die HR-Praxis ein.​
Du arbeitest mit internationalen Teams, IT-Spezialisten und deinem persönlichen Mentor daran, dich zur nächsten Generation von Führungskräften im HR-Bereich zu entwickeln.​
Dein akademisches Fundament:​
Du hast einen sehr guten (Vollzeit-) Master z. B. in BWL, (Wirtschafts-) Informatik, Digitalisierung, Data Science, Personalmanagement oder Arbeits- und Organisationspsychologie abgeschlossen. Themen wie GenAI, HR-Tech, Machine Learning oder Digitalisierung interessieren dich wirklich.​
Deine Begeisterung für HR-Innovationen & Tech:​
Du hast Lust auf technologische Trends, zukunftsweisende HR-Prozesse und strategische Entscheidungen. Generative AI, Machine Learning und HR-Tech-Anwendungen sind für dich keine Pflicht – sondern eine Leidenschaft, die du aktiv im HR-Umfeld einbringen willst.​
Dein Blick für das große Ganze:​
Du willst verstehen, wie Technologie und menschenzentrierte Lösungen zusammenhängen – und wie du an der Schnittstelle von HR und IT echten Mehrwert für globale Teams schaffst.​
Dein Verständnis für Human-centric Leadership:​
Du kannst Menschen begeistern, gehst offen auf andere zu und baust starke, interdisziplinäre Beziehungen auf – denn für dich steht der Mensch bei allen technologischen Innovationen im Mittelpunkt.​
Du denkst strategisch und gestaltest die Zukunft:​
Du hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse, entwickelst kreative und innovative Ideen für GenAI-Anwendungen und hast den Drive, HR-Tools von der ersten Idee bis zur Implementierung umzusetzen.​
Deine kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung:​
Du willst wachsen – fachlich und persönlich. Du bist neugierig, lernst schnell und übernimmst gerne Verantwortung. Vielleicht bringst du sogar schon erste Berufserfahrung, einen MBA oder PhD mit.​
Deine sprachliche Gewandtheit:
Du kommunizierst verhandlungssicher auf Englisch und Deutsch. Du hast bereits Auslandserfahrung von mindestens drei Monaten gesammelt und bringst idealerweise erste praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Tools (z. B. ChatGPT, MidJourney, DALL·E) oder Programmiersprachen mit.​
Warum du es lieben wirst, Teil unserer Community zu sein​
Wir sind tief in das Wachstum unserer Teammitglieder investiert. Wir haben eine Umgebung geschaffen, in der du unterstützt, geschätzt und befähigt wirst, deine beste Arbeit zu leisten. ​

title: Thesis AI Agent for Automated Machine Diagnostics and Root-Cause Analysis
description:
During your thesis, you will build a reliable agent that analyzes a user's machine behavior directly from CAN measurements and derives solutions across calibrations, software bugs, or application/hardware issues.
You will create the agent harness, custom skills, and necessary tools or MCP servers to enable it (e.g. with LangChain).
Furthermore, you will set up automated signal and event detection routines to capture anomalies such as limit violations, oscillations, derating, and error states.
You will prepare appropriate context for the agent, integrating relevant documentation, parameters, and domain knowledge.
Additionally, you will benchmark the agent against established reference cases to assess its accuracy and reproducibility.
Moreover, you will automate the simulation loop by replaying measurements within a virtual test bench (e.g., TPT) to cross-compare simulated dynamics with measured behavior.
Finally, you will document the developed tool and present your findings and methodology to the team.
Education: studies in the field of Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science or comparable

title: GPU Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About PolarGrid
PolarGrid is an early-stage Canadian company that runs managed AI inference. A customer brings a model or a serving image. We run it on dedicated GPUs behind one endpoint, serve each request from the nearest site, and move traffic to the next nearest site when one fails.
Our goal is to make AI inference fast, reliable, and secure for customers running production workloads.
The Role
This role is responsible for scaling PolarGrid's inference network from a handful of sites to a geographically distributed fleet of GPU clusters. The GPU Infrastructure Engineer will own how new sites and nodes come online, from provisioning and burn-in through validation and a staged move into production. They will define when a site is ready for customer traffic, and make sure each new site joins the network without hurting latency or reliability.
A core responsibility is running the global routing layer that sends each request to the best place to serve it. The GPU Infrastructure Engineer will work with live signals such as network latency, capacity and health, and tune routing against real traffic to keep latency low and predictable.
The role also owns reliability across the network. The GPU Infrastructure Engineer will set and track availability targets, build the health checks and automation that detect and route around failing hardware and models, keep recovery fast, and test failure handling regularly.
The GPU Infrastructure Engineer will build the observability, release and network systems needed to run a distributed GPU fleet without operations work growing with every new site. This includes end-to-end tracing and latency alerting, safe staged rollouts, network configuration as code, and security and DDoS protection at the edge.
Requirements
Experience operating distributed systems across multiple sites or regions with high availability targets
Strong networking fundamentals: BGP, DNS, TCP/TLS and load balancing
Hands-on experience running bare-metal GPU fleets: provisioning, burn-in, firmware and node lifecycle
InfiniBand or RDMA networking experience
Experience running LLM inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM, including multi-node serving, cold starts and TTFT
Deep observability skills focused on p95/p99 latency and gray failures, not just uptime
Experience designing failover, graceful degradation and automated recovery
Strong automation and infrastructure-as-code mindset, including CI/CD for infrastructure
Ability to plan capacity on constrained, uneven hardware supply
Experience building internal tooling or control planes, ideally in Go or Rust
Nice to Have
- DDoS mitigation experience
- Running DNS infrastructure at scale
Hardware security: TPM, measured boot or confidential computing
Real-time streaming inference, including voice and audio
Operating remote datacenter sites with on-site technicians
Certificate automation across many domains
- Deterministic simulation testing

title: Software Engineer III — Evaluation
description:
GENERAL OVERVIEW:
Education Advanced, Inc. is a rapidly growing educational technology (Ed-Tech) company in the K-12 industry. Our goal is to create operational software that empowers educators to work more efficiently in specific areas.
Evaluation is our teacher and staff observation and evaluation product. It is a Ruby on Rails application hosted on AWS, and it includes AI-powered features that help educators do their best work. We are hiring a Software Engineer III to own significant parts of the product. This is a small, tight-knit team, so the role carries real breadth: you will work across the Rails application, our AI-powered features, the data integrations that connect Evaluation to other systems, and the cloud infrastructure it all runs on. You will also help others understand how the system works, so documentation and mentoring are part of the job, not something you get to after the sprint. You will start with a structured onboarding period, then help shape where the product and its architecture go next. This is a remote role with core availability during US Central Time business hours.
We foster a supportive, inclusive, and innovation-driven culture where every voice matters and your work directly empowers teachers and students. Join us to grow, collaborate, and build solutions that transform K–12 education.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Roles and Responsibilities
Design, build, ship, and support features across the Evaluation application, from the first product conversation through release and production support.
Build and improve AI-powered product features: integrate large language models (LLMs) into real user workflows, and help design the prompts, safeguards, and quality checks that keep AI output accurate, safe, and useful for educators.
Build and maintain data integrations between Evaluation and other systems, with a focus on reliability and data quality.
Lead technical improvements on the roadmap, such as simplifying configuration, reducing technical debt, and modernizing parts of the application, and sequence that work so delivery keeps moving.
Write clean, high-quality, testable, secure, and maintainable code, and help strengthen our automated testing practices.
Build and operate in AWS using CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and troubleshoot production issues end to end across the application and infrastructure.
Meet FERPA, state student-privacy, and WCAG accessibility requirements as part of normal delivery.
Use AI-assisted development tools as a core part of how you work (planning, coding, testing, code review, and documentation) while checking everything they produce and standing behind every line you ship.
Help shape how the team uses AI in the development lifecycle, including shared conventions, reusable prompts and instructions, and guardrails for safe use.
Partner with Product Management to refine requirements, take part in backlog refinement and sprint planning, and turn specifications into scalable, secure implementations.
Mentor teammates through code review, pairing, and technical planning, and write clear documentation that helps others work confidently in the system.
Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications and Education Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years building and operating production web applications, including recent, hands-on Ruby on Rails experience (Ruby, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS).
Strong relational database skills (MySQL or similar): schema design, indexing, query performance, and safe migrations in a multi-tenant application.
Hands-on experience writing automated tests in Rails (for example, RSpec) at the unit and integration level.
Hands-on experience deploying, running, and debugging applications in AWS, including containers, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure as code.
Solid grasp of secure web development (for example, OWASP Top 10, authentication and authorization, input validation, and secrets management).
Daily, hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools in professional work (for example, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenAI Codex), beyond autocomplete to multi-step work such as building features, refactoring, writing tests, and exploring unfamiliar code.
Skill at directing AI tools: giving clear specs and context, breaking work into small, checkable steps, and using tests and code review to catch output that is wrong, insecure, or made up.
Sound judgment about AI and data safety, including what code and data should never be shared with an AI tool, especially student and educator data.
A track record of owning ambiguous work end to end, from design through delivery and support, without needing it broken down for you.
Comfort working productively in a mature codebase and improving it without stalling delivery.
Excellent written and verbal communication for async, cross-time-zone teamwork, including explaining technical tradeoffs to non-engineers.
Experience working in an Agile team (backlog refinement, sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives).
Core availability during US Central Time business hours.
Authorized to work in the United States.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building LLM-powered features in production: prompt design, testing and evaluating AI output, cost and latency tradeoffs, and safeguards against unsafe or low-quality results.
Experience with managed AI services from a major cloud provider.
Experience building AI tools into a team's development process, such as shared repo instructions, reusable prompts, or custom agents that help AI tools follow team standards.
Experience introducing or expanding automated testing in an existing codebase.
Frontend modernization experience in a server-rendered Rails application (for example, Hotwire, Stimulus, or a component-based approach).
Accessibility remediation experience against WCAG 2.1 AA.
K-12 or public-sector software background, or experience with student information system (SIS) data and student data privacy.
Experience mentoring engineers earlier in their career.
How We Work
Small teams with real ownership: feature branches, a release branch model, frequent deploys, and feature flags for controlled rollout.
AI across the whole lifecycle: We use AI tools throughout R&D, and we keep building them into how we plan, build, test, review, and release software. How we do that is still changing, and you'll help shape it.
You own what you ship: if you can't explain code you submitted, it isn't ready, no matter what wrote it.
Privacy first: student and educator data is handled with care in every tool and every environment.
Salary: $135,000-$155,000

description:

The Cloud Infrastructure Engineer supports the operation, maintenance, automation, and continued modernization of AWS and hybrid-cloud infrastructure supporting federal systems. The engineer will work alongside senior infrastructure and security engineers to implement cloud changes, troubleshoot issues, maintain infrastructure-as-code, remediate vulnerabilities, monitor system health, and improve operational processes.

Troubleshoot networking, operating system, application connectivity, permissions, DNS, and cloud-service issues.
Support vulnerability remediation, patching, configuration compliance, and security-hardening activities.
Assist with cloud migrations, modernization efforts, disaster recovery, and infrastructure lifecycle activities.
Develop scripts and automation to reduce repetitive administrative work.
Maintain technical documentation, diagrams, procedures, and change records.
Participate in incident response and root-cause analysis.
Work with senior engineers to learn cloud architecture, security, networking, automation, and operational best practices.
Gradually assume ownership of cloud services and technical workstreams as experience develops.

Bachelor’s degree in information systems or relevant field and 1-3 years of practical experience in the field

Ability to independently manage assigned work, document technical activities, communicate issues, and seek assistance when appropriate.
Demonstrated self-initiative to build enterprise-like AWS systems and resources that align with well-architected frameworks
Understanding of fundamental networking concepts including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, subnets, and firewalls/security groups, with the ability to apply systematic troubleshooting methods
Basic understanding of infrastructure security concepts such as least privilege, vulnerability remediation, system hardening, and security baselines.
Hands-on experience building solutions with Cloudformation, Terraform, Python, or other tools
Beneficial Qualifications
Cloud related certifications (Solutions Architect, Azure Administrator, etc)
Exposure to CIS Benchmarks, STIGs, or similar security and compliance frameworks

title: Developer
description:
Moodle with us!
We're the world's most popular learning platform, and we’re on a mission to empower educators and learners worldwide with open, flexible, and innovative digital learning solutions. As the world’s most customisable and trusted open-source LMS, we partner with schools, universities, and organisations to create better learning experiences for millions. If you’re ready to make a real impact, and be part of a global movement shaping the future of learning, join us. Let's transform education together!
About the role..
Are you passionate about technology, already building things in your career as a developer? We’re looking for a motivated and curious Developer with 2 to 3 years of experience to join our Platform Solutions team. The team builds, improves and maintains Moodle LMS, the open-source platform all of Moodle’s products are built on. You’ll work on the core LMS alongside experienced developers, and your changes go through Moodle’s open contribution process.
We're building a team that works with AI, not around it. If you've been teaching yourself to build with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or the OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, and you can show us what you've made, we want to hear from you. It matters far more to us what you've built than where (or whether) you studied.
This is a fully remote role and can be offered as a permanent role in India, Indonesia, Vietnam or the Philippines.
At Moodle, no two days will ever be the same, but will involve a mix of:
Collaborating with experienced developers on designing, developing, and implementing software solutions.
Using AI coding agents as part of your everyday workflow: scoping the task, writing a clear spec or prompt, then reviewing, testing and refining what comes back.
Writing clean, well-tested PHP and JavaScript, and being able to explain and defend every line of it, whether you or an agent wrote it first.
Building small automations and internal tools that make the wider team faster.
Participating in code reviews, learning best practices and improving code quality.
Contributing to the full software development lifecycle from concept to deployment and maintenance.
Learning new technologies and tools while solving real-world problems.
Contributing to projects that impact millions of users globally.
What we’re looking for..
Experience with or knowledge of PHP and JavaScript.
Hands-on experience with agentic AI development tools (for example Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or agents you've built yourself with an LLM API). Self-taught absolutely counts: side projects, hackathons, open-source contributions and things you built for fun are all evidence.
Working understanding of how to get good results from these tools: giving an agent the right context, breaking work into verifiable steps, and knowing when the output is wrong.
Judgement about where AI helps and where it doesn't, and a healthy scepticism about code you didn't reason through yourself.
Passion for problem-solving, keen attention to detail and an eagerness to keep learning.
An approachable, collaborative way of working in a global team.
Strong communication and collaboration skills: increasingly, being a strong developer means being able to describe a problem precisely, to people and to machines.
Nice to have, not required: familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol), retrieval-augmented generation, prompt/context engineering, agent evaluation or testing, or having published a tool, plugin or agent of your own.
You don't need a certification or a formal AI qualification for this role. A GitHub repo, a demo video or a blog post explaining something you built will tell us more than any course certificate.
What life at Moodle is like..
Moodle has a globally diverse team with over 280 team members in more than 25 countries around the world. We’ve built a passionate team of hard-working, driven and diverse people from all over the world, united by a shared belief in the ability of our platform to make a positive difference in our world. We respect our colleagues and value an open and innovative workplace filled with integrity and of course a strong focus on education (yes, these are our company values!)
In addition, you can expect:
A genuinely flexible, remote role, working from anywhere in India, Indonesia, Vietnam or the Philippines.
We believe in motivating performance rather than micromanaging it, empowering you to do what you do best.
Gaining new skills by learning from highly skilled peers, along with your own learning and development allowance each year to support your growth.
Work with a global team on a worldwide platform and make a real difference.
As a certified B Corp, we are proud to be part of a global community of mission-driven companies dedicated to using business as a force for good.
Other excellent benefits, like an extra time-off to recharge yourself, give back to a charity or community group, and enjoy a day off for your birthday, ‘choose your own’ benefit options, flexible public holidays, and many more!
Learn more about your new workplace..
Moodle is the world’s most trusted online learning solution, with a growing ecosystem of products and services, including Moodle Workplace, Moodle App, MoodleCloud, and more. The engine of our ecosystem is Moodle LMS, the secure and customisable open-source learning management platform used by well over 300million learners worldwide.
Find out more about us on our website and careers page

Your expertise will directly shape how Grok speaks and understands Uzbek, from pronunciation and natural phrasing to cultural nuance. You will see your work show up in a product used by people around the world.

Annotate, label, and provide feedback on multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, and speech samples using proprietary tools.
Translate and localize text (UI copy, prompts, responses, and other content) from English into Uzbek, with attention to accuracy, natural phrasing, and cultural fit.
Help produce clear, natural audio data that accurately captures linguistic and prosodic details such as intonation, rhythm, and accent.
Collaborate with technical staff to refine annotation guidelines and tools for handling accents, background noise, speech variation, and multilingual audio.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
Proficiency in Uzbek at CEFR C1 level or higher.
English proficiency at CEFR B2 level or higher.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Native proficiency in Uzbek.
English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher.
Experience in one or more of the following areas:
Advanced transcription or audio annotation, with strong attention to accents, prosody, disfluencies, and variable recording quality.
Translation or localization work (especially UI, product copy, or conversational text) between English and Uzbek.
Voice recording, voice acting, podcasting, or related audio production that demonstrates clear delivery and attention to sound quality.
Background in linguistics, phonetics, speech sciences, or hands-on work with speech/audio datasets and AI training data.

Canada
Australia

SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Use proprietary software to provide labels, annotations, recordings, and inputs on projects involving multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, speech samples, and auditory elements in various languages.
Support the delivery of high-quality curated audio data that ensures clear, natural spoken output, accurate representation of linguistic and prosodic details (such as intonation, rhythm, and accent), and professional audio standards.

Comfort providing high-quality voice recordings and feedback on audio samples in multiple languages.
Strong comprehension skills and the ability to make independent judgments on ambiguous or varied audio material, including noisy or accented speech.
Strong communication, interpersonal, analytical, detail-oriented, and organizational skills, with the ability to articulate audio-related feedback effectively.

title: DevOps Engineer | Luma
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics
At Dotmatics, a Siemens company, we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.
We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.
We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.
Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.
Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics
Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.
You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.
We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.
What do we need
Dotmatics is seeking a DevOps Engineer to join our team working on ground-breaking Scientific Software products such as Luma. In this role, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge to help improve our processes, infrastructure and security by applying best practices with the latest technologies. You will be AI fluent and know how AI influences engineering and DevOps
In this role you will get to:
Design and manage CI/CD and deployment pipelines for both AWS-native and Kubernetes-based applications
Provide advice/assistance to the product teams, clarifying requirements for deployment
Collaborate with product teams on cloud and container best practices
Manage IT infrastructure in cloud computing environments
Automation: Use CI tools to automate code changes, builds, testing, and analysis
Monitoring: Monitor performance after release
Develop and improve monitoring systems for automated alerts
Strategy: Design and manage the DevOps infrastructure, pipelines, and processes
SECURITY: Embed security into every stage of the delivery lifecycle (DevSecOps), including automated SAST, DAST, dependency, secrets, and container image scanning in CI/CD pipelines
SECURITY: Implement and enforce least-privilege IAM, network segmentation, encryption in transit and at rest, and secrets management (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, KMS)
SECURITY: Harden Kubernetes clusters and cloud environments using policy-as-code, admission controls, runtime protection, and CIS/NIST benchmarks
SECURITY: Support vulnerability management, incident response, audit readiness, and compliance efforts (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001)
AI: Use AI-assisted tooling to accelerate pipeline development, infrastructure code, troubleshooting, and incident analysis
AI: Apply AI/ML-driven capabilities to monitoring, including anomaly detection, alert noise reduction, and automated root-cause analysis
AI: Build and operate deployment pipelines and infrastructure for AI/ML and LLM-based workloads, including model serving, GPU-enabled clusters, and cost controls
AI: Establish guardrails for responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data privacy, access controls, and review of AI-generated code and configuration
We are looking for people who have 8+ years of experience maintaining high-traffic applications and complex technical infrastructure. You will be someone with a proven background in supporting cloud environments, with hands-on experience translating AWS Well-Architected principles into action.
The key skills we are looking for:
Kubernetes clusters/customer cloud environments
AWS (ECS, EKS, ALB, EC2, S3, RDS, CloudFront, Route53, etc.)
Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi)
CI/CD tools (Octopus Deploy, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, TeamCity, CodePipeline, etc.)
APMs and logging (e.g. Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, ELK, App Insights)
Networking concepts in cloud environments
Software development lifecycle processes/version control
Security: DevSecOps practices, AWS security services (IAM, GuardDuty, Security Hub, WAF, Config, KMS), container and supply chain security (image signing, SBOMs), and security scanning tools (e.g. Trivy, Snyk, SonarQube, Checkov)
Security: Familiarity with Kubernetes security (RBAC, network policies, Pod Security Standards, OPA/Kyverno) and secrets management
AI: Practical experience using AI coding and operations assistants (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude, Amazon Q) to improve engineering productivity
AI: Understanding of how to deploy and operate AI/ML workloads (e.g. Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, model-serving on Kubernetes) and observe their performance and cost
AI: Awareness of AI-specific risks such as prompt injection, data leakage, and insecure AI-generated code
You may also have:
Scripting languages (e.g. Python, Bash)
Linux administration and networking (e.g. HTTP/2)
Microservice and serverless architectures
Experience with GitOps tooling (e.g. Argo CD, Flux)
Experience building internal tooling or agents that apply AI to DevOps workflows (e.g. automated incident triage, ChatOps)
Relevant certifications (e.g. AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Security Specialty, CKA/CKS)
Databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB)
Exposure to AI-enabled tooling or workflows, with openness to incorporating AI into day-to-day work
Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.
By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information.
Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

description:
Description
AWS Cloud Engineer
Location: US / Canada (Eastern Time) - Home based
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
About AllCloud
AllCloud is a leader in amplifying organizations’ cloud potential through AI. With a track record of hundreds of successful migrations and implementations across AWS and Salesforce, AllCloud has developed strategies and solutions that enable businesses of all sizes to remain at the forefront of innovation.
AllCloud is a leader in AI-led professional and managed services. As an AWS Premier and audited managed services Partner, and Salesforce Consulting partner, AllCloud provides comprehensive AI-led cloud journey support, from initial migration to ongoing management through our Engage Managed Services. Our expertise ensures that clients remain aligned with ecosystem best practices while focusing on their core business growth.
AllCloud serves clients across the globe with offices in EMEA and North America. www.allcloud.io
﻿
Job Summary
AllCloud is seeking an AWS Cloud Engineer to design, build, and deploy highly scalable, reliable, and secure cloud environments for our customers. In this role, you will focus on delivering complex cloud projects, including large-scale migrations from on-premises data centers to AWS, containerized application deployment (including Amazon EKS), building new landing zones, and implementing infrastructure-as-code using modern automation frameworks. You will be responsible for setting up, maintaining, and evolving AWS architectures; developing automation to streamline delivery; ensuring robust monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting practices; and leveraging cutting-edge AWS services to help customers achieve their business goals. This position is hands-on, customer-facing, and integral to driving successful AWS delivery engagements.
Requirements
Summary of Key Responsibilities
Architect, design, deploy, and maintain scalable, highly available, and secure AWS infrastructure for project needs (e.g., compute, storage, networking, database).
Lead or participate in cloud migrations: lifting and shifting on-premises workloads, re-architecting to cloud-native services.
Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK.
Implement CI/CD pipelines (for example via AWS CodePipeline / AWS CodeBuild / Jenkins / GitLab CI) to automate deployment workflows.
Implement serverless solutions using AWS Lambda, Step Functions, and integrate event-driven architectures where appropriate.
Containerize applications (Docker) and orchestrate microservices using AWS container platform services, with a strong focus on Amazon EKS, ECS, and Fargate.
Ensure monitoring, logging, alerting, tracing of AWS resources and applications using tools like CloudWatch, X-Ray, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/EFK stack.
Apply best practices around security: IAM policies, least privilege, encryption (at rest/in transit), network segmentation (VPCs, subnets), Web Application Firewall (WAF), GuardDuty, AWS Shield, etc.
Implement backup, disaster recovery and high availability strategies; manage data redundancies, snapshots, multi-AZ / multi-region architectures.
Optimize cost & performance: right-sizing resources, identifying waste, designing for efficiency.
Troubleshoot, debug, and resolve issues in cloud infrastructure and services; conduct root cause analyses.
Maintain documentation for architectures, configurations, standard operating procedures, runbooks.
Engage with cross-functional teams: developers, QA, operations, security/compliance, and project managers to ensure successful delivery.
Communicate proactively and effectively with clients to understand technical needs, provide progress updates, and articulate complex solutions clearly.
Apply critical thinking and strategic problem-solving to evaluate trade-offs, identify root causes, and design robust cloud architectures.
Stay up to date on the latest AWS services, features, industry best practices; evaluate new technologies and recommend improvements.
Perform deep OS-level troubleshooting and system administration across both Linux and Windows environments operating in the cloud.
Summary of Requirements & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or relevant field (or equivalent work experience).

title: AI Engineer I/II/III
description:
At EQT, you won't just do a job, you'll help shape our future. Through Transparent Leadership, you'll work alongside leaders who value collaboration and ensure every voice is heard. Through Connected Impact, you'll see how your work influences critical business decisions and drives value across our operations. Through Supported Growth, you'll have opportunities to expand your skills through cross-functional collaboration, development opportunities, and career advancement. Join our Qrew!
EQT is building a fleet of AI agents that work alongside our people, and we need an AI Engineer to help it grow. You'll join an AI team that builds the shared tools agents rely on, configures and deploys the agents themselves, and keeps the whole fleet healthy once it's live.
Our agents already run in production on Microsoft Foundry, posting into Salesforce and the enterprise systems our people use every day. The next step is scale: many more agents, built faster, with business users helping tune them.
As an AI Engineer, you build and maintain the capabilities our agents run on, and you monitor and optimize the agent fleet once it's in production. You set up the configuration for each prompt agent and customize its tools. Then you hand off to AI Specialists and domain experts, who test against real cases and tune the prompts until the agent is right.
When reasoning alone can't do the job reliably, you build a pro-code hosted agent or specialized tooling. That's the exception, not the plan.
Who thrives here:
You think agentically. You trust reasoning models to do most of the heavy lifting, and you reach for deterministic code where the outcome must be guaranteed, not by default.
You build for flexibility. You'd rather ship an agent that improves as models get better and cheaper than hardcode every scenario and fall behind.
You favor progress over perfection. You'd rather get many useful agents live and improve them than polish one forever.
You make others better. You enjoy building the tools and patterns that let business users and new builders do more on their own.
You're excited about where AI is going. You follow the field, try new models and tools as they land, and want to help an organization change how it works.
The AI Engineer I/II/III responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Build and maintain shared agent tools and capabilities.
Configure Foundry prompt agents: instructions, model selection, tool assignments, permissions, and guardrails, ready for others to test and tune.
Customize and extend tools when an agent needs something the shared set doesn't yet cover.
Partner with AI Specialists and domain experts as they test against real cases, and coach them on prompt design and evaluation.
Deploy agents and monitor the fleet through the Foundry control plane: evaluations, monitoring and alerts, audit trail, and cost.
Optimize agents in production, and recognize when a deployment is drifting or needs tighter guardrails, better data, or a narrower scope.
Build pro-code hosted agents or specialized tooling when review shows a prompt agent can't do the job reliably.
Ensure agents adhere to our security and identity standards.
Help shape the Agent Factory standards and share what you learn, so the next agent is faster to build than the last.
Stay current with models, agent frameworks, and Foundry features, and bring forward ideas that move more work from code to reasoning.
Required Experience and Skills:
Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline (computer science, engineering, information systems, or similar), or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, data engineering, or AI/ML roles.
Hands-on experience building LLM-based agents or applications: prompt design, tool calling, retrieval, and evaluating outputs against real cases.
Solid software engineering fundamentals in Python, including git, code review, testing, and working with APIs.
Working experience with Microsoft Azure or a similar cloud platform, including identity, permissions, and secrets management.
Comfort working across enterprise systems and data, including SQL and integrating with platforms like Salesforce and Databricks.
Judgment about when code is the right answer versus when a well-designed prompt and the right tools are simpler and just as successful.
Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to business partners and coach non-engineers as they test and tune agents.
Preferred Experience and Skills:
Experience with Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry): prompt agents, hosted agents, tools, evaluations, and the control plane.
Exposure to agent frameworks and protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or similar.
Working knowledge of Salesforce (configuration, security model, Flow) and the Databricks ecosystem (Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL).
Experience operating AI in production: monitoring, evaluation harnesses, cost tracking, and responsible AI practices such as PII handling, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop review.

As a Data Engineer, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of data — from ingesting raw event streams and third-party feeds to building well-modelled, highly reliable datasets that power dashboards, predictive models, and customer journey orchestration. This is a high-impact, hands-on role where you will work at the intersection of product, analytics, and backend engineering. Pipeline Development & Reliability
Design, build, and maintain production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest data from APIs, databases, event streams (Kafka/Pub-Sub), and flat files into the central data warehouse.

Data Modelling & Warehouse Design

Design slowly changing dimensions (SCD Type 1/2), bridge tables, and fact tables optimised for analytical query patterns.
Enforce partitioning, clustering, and materialised view strategies to keep warehouse costs under control while maintaining sub-second query performance.
Code Quality & Engineering Best Practices
Write clean, modular, well-tested Python and SQL code. Follow DRY principles, use version control (Git), and participate in peer code reviews.
Build reusable transformation frameworks using dbt or equivalent tooling, with proper documentation and testing at every layer (staging → intermediate → mart).
Containerise data services with Docker and automate deployments via CI/CD pipelines (GitHub
Actions / GitLab CI).
BI, Visualization & Analytics
Build interactive dashboards and analytical tools using Streamlit, enabling stakeholders to explore metrics, run ad-hoc analyses, and make data-driven decisions without engineering dependency.

Translate raw data into compelling visual narratives using libraries like Plotly, Matplotlib, or Altair; present findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Collaboration & Communication
Partner with product managers, analysts, and data scientists to understand data needs and proactively identify gaps in current data coverage.
Document data lineage, transformation logic, SLAs, and known limitations in a shared knowledge base to enable self-service analytics.
Contribute to internal engineering guilds, knowledge-sharing sessions, and post-incident reviews for pipeline failures.

Strong SQL skills with expertise in complex queries, performance optimization, and cost-efficient design on cloud data warehouses (BigQuery, Redshift).
Strong Python scripting for data ingestion, transformation, and validation, with hands-on experience in Pandas, SQLAlchemy, APIs, and automation.
ETL/ELT- End-to-end ownership of data pipelines, including ingestion, transformation, and loading, with understanding of incremental loads, and backfills.
Data Modelling- Ability to design dimensional and transactional data models (star/snowflake, SCDs) and translate business needs into optimized table structures.

title: AI Studio Coach- Agentic AI
description:
Agentic AI Coach
About Break Through Tech
Break Through Tech transforms how tech talent is discovered, developed, and connected to opportunity in the age of AI. Working across higher education and industry, Break Through Tech delivers programs nationwide and integrates technical training, work-based learning, mentorship, and career readiness with deep employer partnerships to create more effective and scalable routes into early tech careers. Break Through Tech is actively shaping the field of early tech talent development by identifying what works, translating those insights into replicable models, and helping define more consistent approaches to how talent is prepared, assessed, and hired across institutions and employers.
At a moment when AI is reshaping every aspect of work and society, Break Through Tech’s mission is urgent: to ensure that the people who build what comes next — and who are in the room where the most consequential technology decisions of our time get made — look like the world they will shape. Learn more about our work at.
Position Summary
We are seeking several subject matter experts to partner with Break Through Tech program staff to deliver our Agentic AI programs for up to 500 undergraduate fellows. Agentic AI is offered at two levels, Beginner and Advanced. Coaches will be matched to a level based on their experience with Agentic AI and staffing needs.
For a long time, chatbots were the biggest thing in AI. Now companies are building them into something more powerful: agents that work together to plan, use tools, hand off work, and take action. That shift is creating fast-growing demand for engineers who can design, evaluate, and deploy these systems.
The new 16-week Agentic AI program builds on fellows' foundation in machine learning and Python. Many have completed our rigorous 9-week Machine Learning Foundations course and a 3-month industry-sponsored AI project. Fellows learn to build agents, extend them with tools and knowledge, measure how well they perform, and ship systems that hold up in production.
With expert guidance and support from their Coaches, fellows will work in teams to build agents from ideation onward. They will build agentic systems in LangGraph, stress-test them with systematic evaluations, trace every decision in LangSmith, and use what they learn to make their systems faster, cheaper, and more reliable. They will then deploy to the cloud and present at a final showcase.
Across 4 units, fellows move from agent fundamentals through architecture, evaluation, and deployment, learning the practices professional AI engineers use. Asynchronous coursework will be completed before monthly virtual Workshops and Maker Days, where teams build and troubleshoot together.
Coaches for this Specialization will each support 8–10 project teams (about 40 fellows). Coaches will be expected to facilitate live virtual events end-to-end, provide technical mentorship and code review, hold regular team check-ins, and grade and give feedback on project deliverables.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
The essential duties of this role are grouped into these categories, with the approximate percentage of time spent on each category indicated below.
Event Facilitation (30%)
Facilitate 4 Workshops (1.5 hours each, one per month) from start to finish for your assigned fellows, leading code demos and guided project working sessions.
Facilitate 4 Maker Days (3 hours each, one per month) from start to finish, leading build-sprint structure, checking milestone progress, and troubleshooting technical issues live.
Prepare for each Workshop and Maker Day you are facilitating.
Maintain attendance records for Workshops, Maker Days, and team check-ins.
Technical Support (25%)
Provide technical mentorship on agent design, RAG and tool integration, evaluation and observability (LangSmith), and cloud deployment and containerization. Advanced Agentic AI Coaches will also provide mentorship on multi-agent architecture and coordination patterns.
Review code and conduct debugging sessions to troubleshoot complex technical issues.
Find and recommend additional resources to support your teams' projects as needed.
Attend and actively engage in twice-monthly Community of Practice meetings with other Coaches and program staff, to share ideas and troubleshoot together.
Team Check-Ins & Progress Monitoring (25%)
Hold a recurring check-in at least once a month with each of your 8–10 assigned teams to monitor progress and provide feedback.
Monitor team progress and intervene to address technical blockers or team dynamics issues.
Partner with Break Through Tech program staff to manage unresolved issues affecting project success.
Conduct outreach to at-risk fellows, which may include 1:1s and post-meeting follow-ups.
Assessment & Feedback (20%)
Grade unit and event deliverables for all of your assigned teams using provided rubrics.
Track deliverable submissions and follow up with teams that have not submitted.
Provide constructive technical feedback on project milestones and presentations.
Observe final presentations and provide meaningful feedback.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Solid knowledge of agent architecture, including tool calling, RAG, and memory. Advanced Agentic AI Coaches will also need solid knowledge of multi-agent coordination patterns, including supervisor/orchestrator workflows, agent handoffs, and agents-as-tools.
Comfortable reading, writing, and debugging Python code.
Ability to troubleshoot code and debug complex systems.
Excellent communication and facilitation skills (including evaluating and giving feedback on technical work).
Comfort facilitating a live session for a group of about 40 fellows.
Ability to thrive in a virtual work environment.
Commitment to developing inclusive and equitable working relationships with fellows from a variety of backgrounds, volunteers, other Coaches, and program staff.
Education and/or Experience
Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in computer science, data science, or a related field. An advanced degree is a plus.
Strong background in AI/ML with hands-on experience in agent development.
Experience personally building an agent with tools and/or RAG, and evaluating its performance. Advanced Agentic AI Coaches will also need experience building a multi-agent system or a single-agent system with advanced tool routing, and running systematic evaluations on agent performance.
Hands-on experience with LangChain and LangGraph. Advanced Agentic AI Coaches will also need hands-on experience with LangGraph subgraphs, parallel execution, and multi-agent coordination patterns.
Hands-on experience with RAG systems, API integrations, and deploying applications to cloud platforms.
Experience with evaluation and observability/tracing tools, particularly LangSmith.
Experience with deployment and containerization (Docker, cloud platforms).
Prior teaching, tutoring, or mentoring experience, including coaching or leading a team through an ambiguous, open-ended technical project.
Experience giving feedback on presentations or public speaking coaching.
Prior Break Through Tech and/or Machine Learning Foundations experience is a plus.
Important Notes
This is a part-time, remote, temporary position beginning on Monday, January 4th, 2027 and ending on Monday, May 20th, 2027.
Estimated time commitment: 15-20 hours/week. Actual weekly hours will vary depending on program activities.
This role is not eligible for benefits.
This role is open to any eligible candidate across the US.
Visa sponsorship (including H-1B) is not available. Candidates authorized to work through F-1 CPT or OPT are welcome to apply.
Pay rate: $35 per hour.
Coaches will be required to participate in about 10 hours of pre-program training in early January 2027.
Coaches will be required to be available to facilitate 8 events (four 90-minute Workshops and four 4-hour Maker Days, including Final Presentations) on to-be-determined dates, from January-May, 2027.

title: Applied AI Engineer
description:
About Dwelly
Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. Its growing network of agencies provides its AI with real-world data, continuous feedback, and control over complete workflows, making exceptional service the standard for landlords and tenants. Today, Dwelly operates more than 15,000 properties and $470 million in GMV, making it one of the UK’s ten largest lettings operators. The company has raised $263 million.
We’re a fast-growing, product-focused company, backed by top-tier investors and led by a team with deep experience in real estate, technology, and operations.
Position Summary
We’re looking for an Applied AI Engineer to help build the agentic infrastructure that powers automation across Dwelly. Our growth model is acquisition. Every agency we acquire brings new operational workflows, legacy processes, and manual work. If we manage each new agency manually, the economics of the model break. Our ability to scale depends on turning complex operational processes into reliable AI-driven and automated systems.
We already have successful AI-driven flows running in Tenant Find and Property Management. They work and deliver real business results. But they were built quickly and as separate systems.
The next challenge is to bring these approaches together: build reusable agentic infrastructure, establish a robust evaluation and observability layer, and create systems that allow us to automate new workflows quickly and reliably as Dwelly scales.
This is not an AI research role. You will be building AI systems that operate inside a real business and are expected to work reliably in production.
We’re hiring remotely across the UK, Ireland, and European time zones. Candidates should be based within these regions/time zones to enable effective collaboration with the wider team.
Key Responsibilities
1. Agentic infrastructure
Design and build the core primitives behind our agentic systems, including memory, context management, tool-calling, orchestration, and feedback loops.
Move us from one-off AI solutions toward reusable infrastructure where new workflows can be introduced quickly and with predictable reliability.
2. Evaluation & observability
Build the evaluation framework that allows us to understand how our agents perform and why they succeed or fail.
Make testing, tracing, debugging, and evaluating AI systems as fundamental to our engineering process as unit testing traditional software.
Develop the systems that allow us to confidently assess an agentic workflow before deploying it into production.
3. Agentic development
Push forward how we use LLMs to build software itself.
Create workflows where coding agents and specialized subagents can explore repositories, implement changes, review architecture, check conventions, run evaluations, and iterate with minimal human coordination.
Use agentic engineering workflows extensively in your own day-to-day development.
4. Orchestration
Design systems where specialized agents, tools, deterministic software, and humans work together effectively.
Understand when a problem should be solved with an LLM, when traditional software is the better solution, and when multiple coordinated agents can materially improve the outcome.
5. Operational automation
Act as the bridge between complex operational workflows and engineering.
Work closely with our operational and product teams to understand how work actually happens across acquired agencies, identify the highest-leverage opportunities for automation, and turn them into reliable production systems.
6. Architectural influence
Help define the architectural patterns we use for agentic systems as the company scales.
You won’t be joining as engineer #20 on an established AI platform. You will be an early core member of the team with significant influence over our technical approach, tooling, and engineering standards.
Qualifications and Preferred Background
Strong software engineering background with experience independently delivering complex systems from idea through to production
Hands-on experience building AI or agentic systems that have operated in production
Experience dealing with real-world AI challenges such as reliability, latency, context management, failure modes, evaluation, and observability
Strong understanding of agents, tool use, structured outputs, context management, orchestration, evaluation, and feedback loops
Advanced practical use of modern LLMs — not simply using ChatGPT or Claude occasionally, but understanding how to build reliable workflows around probabilistic systems
Experience using coding agents and agentic development workflows as part of your own engineering process
Experience decomposing complex engineering tasks across agents or specialized subagents and designing mechanisms for them to verify and improve their outputs
Strong architectural judgment and ability to decide when to use LLMs, deterministic software, human intervention, or a combination of approaches
Experience with TypeScript / Node.js, or strong experience building AI systems in Python with the ability and willingness to apply that knowledge in a TypeScript-first environment
High autonomy, ownership, and comfort making decisions under ambiguity
Strong product judgment and ability to connect technical decisions to operational and business outcomes
Strong communication skills and fluency in English
Startup mentality: resilience, adaptability, and ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment
What We Don't Mean by “AI Experience”
For this role, AI experience does not mean:
Using ChatGPT to generate snippets of code
Adding a single LLM API call to an application
Building a prompt wrapper and calling it an agent
Blindly accepting whatever a coding agent generates
We are looking for engineers who think in terms of agents, tools, context, orchestration, evaluation, feedback loops, and human-machine collaboration — and who already apply these concepts in their day-to-day engineering work.
What Success Looks Like
Within your first 12 months:
Reliability: We can deploy a new agentic workflow and understand how it will perform before it reaches production because we have robust evaluation and observability systems in place.
Speed: Integrating processes from newly acquired agencies takes days rather than weeks because we have a standardized library of reusable agentic primitives.
Efficiency: A significant amount of repetitive operational work has been automated, allowing our teams to focus on the areas where human judgment and interaction create the most value.
Engineering leverage: Agentic development workflows materially increase the speed and quality at which our engineering team can build, test, and evolve software.
Technology Stack
TypeScript (Primary) · Node.js · PostgreSQL · LLM Orchestration · Agentic Workflows
Why This Might Not Be for You
This role is probably not the right fit if:
You primarily want to research new models, read the latest papers, or train custom models. We are pragmatic builders rather than an AI research lab.
You prefer working from a clearly defined backlog where someone else determines what should be built.
You enjoy prototyping AI systems but are less interested in the less glamorous work required to make them reliable — evaluation, logging, error handling, observability, infrastructure, and operational edge cases.
You see AI primarily as a feature rather than a new way of designing and building software systems.
Compensation and benefits
The role is fully remote, providing flexibility and enabling seamless collaboration with our geographically distributed team
Competitive salary with the potential for equity options based on performance, recognising exceptional contributions to our integration success
What is it like being a Dwell-er
Feel free to check out Dwelly Core Principles. That’s about what we believe in, how we operate and make decisions
What we offer is not a fancy office or a static workplace. Instead, this is solving one of the world’s most complex problems in the largest consumer industry in the world (residential rentals), to improve the experience for over 30% of households (more than 5 million in the UK, and over 100 million including EU and US) that live in rental homes
This is about disrupting the largest, most antiquated industry in the world, with one of the strongest operational and technical teams that exist in the UK and the EU. We work hard, and we shoot for extremely ambitious results. But we want people to be proud of what they’ve built and be able to look back and say one day “hell yeah, that was me that did it all”
Customer obsession rather than competitive focus
Passion for invention
Operational excellence
Long-term thinking
By applying for this position, you consent to the processing and storage of your personal data for recruitment purposes for up to 365 days, in accordance with our data retention policy and applicable data protection laws.

Infrastruktur für produktive KI-Anwendungen bauen und betreiben – von der Dev-Umgebung über CI/CD bis zum stabilen Betrieb beim Kunden und außerdem:

Sicherheit und Compliance sicherstellen: Secrets- und Zugriffsmanagement, Guardrails, Nachvollziehbarkeit nach EU AI Act.
Kunden bei Architektur- und Betriebsentscheidungen beraten – als technischer Sparringspartner*, nicht als Kundenmanager*.

MLOps-/LLMOps-Patterns im echten Kundenbetrieb statt im Lehrbuch.
Wie man KI-Systeme so baut, dass sie den EU AI Act überstehen, statt ihn nachträglich zu reparieren.
Den Sprung vom PoC zur produktiven, kosten- und latenzbewussten Plattform.

Mehrjährige Erfahrung in Entwicklung und Betrieb von Software.
Senior-Rolle: mehrjährige Praxis im Design und Betrieb produktiver Systeme
Solide DevOps-Basis: Container/Kubernetes, CI/CD, agiles Entwicklungsumfeld.

Python plus mindestens eine weitere Sprache (Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, C# oder Shell).

Wer beim PoC aufhört und Produktionsbetrieb für das Problem von jemand anderem hält.

Technologiebandbreite statt Monokultur: Machine Learning, LLM-Anwendungen und eigene Agentenplattformen – je nach Problem, nicht je nach Hausstandard.

UNITY ist die Managementberatung für Innovation und digitale Transformation. Dabei setzen wir insbesondere auf Künstliche Intelligenz als Schlüsseltechnologie für Effizienz und Wachstum.
